definitions.definition: X=ℝ^n, identified with EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), with its standard real inner product and Lebesgue measure.
V=ℝ^m, identified with EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m), with its standard real inner product.
Z=X×ℝ with its product real normed space structure.
Ω={(y,r)∈Z:r>0}, the open positive-time spacetime domain.
Uext(y,r)=u(y,r) if r>0, and Uext(y,r)=0∈V otherwise. This is a total representative only; its defining expression asserts no smoothness or regularity.
τ=(0,1)∈X×ℝ, the constant time direction.
For each j∈Fin n, σ(j)=(ε_j,0), where ε_j∈X is the standard coordinate vector with jth coordinate 1 and all other coordinates 0. The printed sums j=1,…,n use the equivalent one-based indexing.

For any real normed spaces W₀,W₁, total F₀:W₀→W₁, v₀∈W₀ and z₀∈W₀, Ddir(v₀,F₀)(z₀)=(fderiv ℝ F₀ z₀)(v₀). Here fderiv is the Fréchet derivative when one exists and the zero continuous linear map otherwise. D_v F denotes this operation. A formula using it grants no differentiability.

u_t=Ddir(τ,Uext). At positive times this notation represents the time partial derivative of u; identifying the Fréchet and ordinary derivatives is a proof obligation, not a property granted by this definition.
For j∈Fin n, u_j(j)=Ddir(σ(j),Uext). In formulas u_j or ∂_{x_j}u denotes its jth member, and its agreement with the spatial partial derivative at positive times is to be proved.
u_tt=Ddir(τ,u_t).
For j∈Fin n, u_jj(j)=Ddir(σ(j),u_j(j)).
For j∈Fin n, u_tj(j)=Ddir(σ(j),u_t). The notation ∂_{x_j}u_t refers to this field. The equality Ddir(τ,u_j(j))=u_tj(j) at positive times requires proof.
Δ_xu(z)=Σ_{j∈Fin n} u_jj(j)(z), the componentwise spatial Laplacian.
e(z)=‖u_t(z)‖²+Σ_{j∈Fin n}‖u_j(j)(z)‖². The spatial sum is the Frobenius square of the spatial gradient. Norms are Euclidean; there is no factor 1/2.

E(r)=∫_{X} e(x,r) dx with Euclidean Lebesgue measure. This uses the total real Bochner-integral convention (zero for a nonintegrable integrand). Integrability at every positive time must be proved so that this is the actual finite energy integral required by the theorem.
T(z)=⟪u_t(z),u_tt(z)⟫, using the real Euclidean inner product on V.
B_j(j)(z)=⟪u_t(z),u_jj(j)(z)⟫.
e_t=Ddir(τ,e). The notation ∂_t e means the ordinary time derivative of the spatial section when it exists; its agreement with this field at positive times is a proof obligation.

inputs.statement: Let n,m≥1 be integers, X=ℝ^n and V=ℝ^m with their Euclidean structures, and u:X×(0,∞)→V jointly C∞. Let q∈V be fixed with ‖q‖=1. For r>0 write u_t=∂_t u, u_j=∂_{x_j}u, u_tt=∂²_tu, u_jj=∂²_{x_j}u, Δ_xu=Σ_{j=1}^n u_jj, e(x,r)=‖u_t(x,r)‖²+Σ_j‖u_j(x,r)‖² and E(r)=∫_X e(x,r)dx, using Lebesgue measure and Frobenius gradient square.
For every x∈ℝ^n and t>0, ‖u(x,t)‖=1 and there exists a real scalar a such that u_tt(x,t)−Σ_{j=1}^n u_jj(x,t)=a u(x,t). No regularity is assumed for any selection of these pointwise scalar witnesses.

inputs.statement: For every jointly smooth sphere-valued map u:ℝ^n×(0,∞)→ℝ^m with n,m≥1 and pointwise normal acceleration u_tt−Σ_j u_jj=a u for a real pointwise witness a, at every x∈ℝ^n and t>0 one has ⟪u,u_t⟫=0 and ⟪u_t,u_tt−Σ_j u_jj⟫=0. No regularity of the scalar witnesses is needed.

Let n,m≥1 and let u:ℝ^n×(0,∞)→ℝ^m be jointly smooth and equal to a fixed q outside a common compact spatial set on each closed positive-time slab. Define u_t,u_j,u_tt,u_jj, e=‖u_t‖²+Σ_j‖u_j‖² and the products T=⟪u_t,u_tt⟫, A_j=⟪u_j,∂_{x_j}u_t⟫, B_j=⟪u_t,u_jj⟫ and H_j=⟪u_t,u_j⟫. These fields and ∂_t e are jointly smooth at positive times. For every t₀>0 there is a compact C⊂ℝ^n such that all positive-order derivatives of u and all these scalar fields vanish for x∉C and r∈(t₀/2,3t₀/2). Their spatial sections there are continuous, compactly supported and Lebesgue integrable. Also ∂_t u_j=∂_{x_j}u_t everywhere at positive times.

This derivative assertion is local on (0,∞), independent of any extension to nonpositive times.

For n,m≥1 and a jointly smooth u:ℝ^n×(0,∞)→ℝ^m equal to a fixed q outside a common compact spatial set on every closed positive-time slab, for every t>0 and j∈{1,…,n}, both real products in the identity ∫_{ℝ^n}⟪u_j,∂_{x_j}u_t⟫(x,t)dx=−∫_{ℝ^n}⟪u_t,u_jj⟫(x,t)dx are integrable and the identity holds.

output.statement:
A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
correction.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.

argument.text: Work with the original data H001,H002,H003: n,m≥1, jointly smooth u, the fixed unit q, the unit constraint and pointwise normal acceleration, and common compact support of the perturbation from q on every closed positive-time slab. This is exactly the selected interpretation of spatial compact support. Fix arbitrary t0 and assume L1: t0>0. N002 and N003 apply to these data: e(·,t0) and T(·,t0), every A_j(·,t0) and B_j(·,t0) are integrable, and E has ordinary derivative ∫_X(2T+2Σ_j A_j)(x,t0)dx at t0. By density integrability, the total integral convention in D016 coincides here with the actual finite energy integral.

produces.statement: At t0 the spatial sections e,T,A_j,B_j are integrable; E is the actual finite energy integral, and HasDerivAt E (∫_X(2T+2Σ_j A_j)(x,t0)dx) t0.

argument.text: All operations here involve finitely many integrable real sections from F001. Finite sums and constant multiples remain integrable: their absolute values are bounded by the finite sum of the absolute values of the summands, multiplied by the absolute constants, and the corresponding measurability and finite-integral conditions follow. E018 splits the integral into the 2T part and the 2Σ_j A_j part. E017 with c=2 extracts each factor 2, and E016 moves the finite spatial sum through its integral. Hence the derivative value in F001 is 2∫_X T(x,t0)dx+2Σ_j∫_X A_j(j)(x,t0)dx. There is no limiting infinite sum.

produces.statement: HasDerivAt E (2∫_X T(x,t0)dx+2Σ_{j∈Fin n}∫_X A_j(j)(x,t0)dx) t0.

argument.text: N004 at t0 gives ∫_X A_j(j)(x,t0)dx=−∫_X B_j(j)(x,t0)dx for each j∈Fin n, with both integrands integrable. Substitute these finitely many equalities into F002 and distribute the finite minus sign. The derivative value is therefore 2∫T−2Σ_j∫B_j.

produces.statement: HasDerivAt E (2∫_X T(x,t0)dx−2Σ_{j∈Fin n}∫_X B_j(j)(x,t0)dx) t0.

argument.text: For every x∈X, N001 gives ⟪u_t,u_tt−Δ_xu⟫(x,t0)=0. Expand the finite Laplacian sum and use real inner-product bilinearity. It yields T(x,t0)=Σ_j B_j(j)(x,t0). Both sides are integrable by F001 and finite integrability closure. Integrating this pointwise equality, then applying E016 to the finite family B_j(·,t0), gives ∫_X T(x,t0)dx=Σ_j∫_X B_j(j)(x,t0)dx. No choice of scalar or derivative of such a choice is used in this step.

Substitute F004 into F003: the derivative value equals twice the same finite real sum minus twice that sum, hence is 0. Thus HasDerivAt E 0 t0, which states ordinary differentiability and E'(t0)=0. F001 already establishes integrability of e(·,t0). Discharge L1 into t0>0 and universally quantify t0 to obtain all three required conclusions for every positive time. Definitions D014–D016 retain the componentwise Laplacian, the Frobenius spatial gradient square, Euclidean Lebesgue measure, and coefficient 1 on each energy square. The original parameter ranges and every hypothesis are retained. No conclusion at time zero or extra assertion about a globally chosen scalar is needed. This proves the full selected target P.
